shared_context.topic: Lyme disease progression prevention with antibiotics

snippets.output: The effectiveness of antibiotics in preventing the progression of Lyme disease is a topic of ongoing debate, but antibiotics are effective in treating the early stages of Lyme disease and can prevent Lyme disease from progressing to its later stages.
snippets.pattern_notes: Debate framing followed by conclusions about effectiveness; conclusion + supporting claims.

snippets.output: In the early stages of Lyme disease, oral antibiotics such as doxycycline are effective in treating the infection and preventing the development of late Lyme disease.
snippets.pattern_notes: Two parallel properties of doxycycline in early Lyme: treats infection and prevents progression.

snippets.output: For patients with early disseminated Lyme disease, especially early disseminated Lyme disease with neurologic findings, parenteral antibiotic therapy such as ceftriaxone may be necessary.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates indication scenarios for parenteral ceftriaxone in early disseminated Lyme.

snippets.output: Treatment of late Lyme disease can be challenging, and some patients with late Lyme disease may require multiple courses of antibiotics and the addition of anti-inflammatory agents.
snippets.pattern_notes: Lists features of late Lyme treatment: challenging, multiple courses, anti-inflammatories.

snippets.output: Even with treatment, some patients with Lyme disease may experience persistent or recurrent symptoms, which can be attributed to chronic inflammation, autoimmunity, or fibromyalgia.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates possible causes of persistent symptoms (inflammation, autoimmunity, fibromyalgia).

snippets.output: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommend treating Lyme disease with antibiotics for 14 days for early disease and for up to 4 weeks for late disease.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel CDC duration recommendations for early vs late disease.

snippets.output: Some studies suggest that shorter courses of antibiotics may be effective in preventing the progression of Lyme disease.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single self-contained claim about shorter antibiotic courses.

snippets.output: Antibiotics are effective in treating the early stages of Lyme disease and can prevent Lyme disease from progressing to later stages, although the optimal treatment duration and regimen for Lyme disease remain a topic of ongoing research and debate.
snippets.pattern_notes: Conclusions about antibiotic effectiveness paired with caveat about ongoing debate over optimal regimen.
